\chapter{Synthesis --- Reading a Paragraph}
\label{ch:sintesis-ocho}
\hlchaptermodality{65}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read a paragraph of Spanish I was never taught.}

I can read a paragraph of Spanish I was never taught.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — reading a paragraph}

\label{lesson:ES-C09-sintesis-ocho}



\begin{quote}
Decode \emph{estación}. (\textbf{Station} — the \emph{e-} off the front, the \emph{-ción} to \emph{-tion} at the back.)

Now a whole paragraph.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Read it slowly. \textbf{Not one of these words appears anywhere else in this book.}

\begin{quote}
\emph{La comunidad literaria tiene una tradición extraordinaria. Su estructura es} \emph{voluntaria, evidentemente, pero la actividad es enorme.}
\end{quote}

Now check yourself:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{what you saw} & \textbf{how you got it} \\
\midrule
\emph{comunidad} & \emph{-dad} $\to$ \textbf{-ty} \\
\emph{literaria} & \emph{-ario}, agreeing $\to$ \textbf{-ary} \\
\emph{tradición} & \emph{-ción} $\to$ \textbf{-tion} \\
\emph{extraordinaria} & \emph{-ario}, agreeing $\to$ \textbf{-ary} \\
\emph{estructura} & take the \emph{e-} off $\to$ \textbf{structure} \\
\emph{voluntaria} & \emph{-ario}, agreeing $\to$ \textbf{-ary} \\
\emph{evidentemente} & \emph{-mente} $\to$ \textbf{-ly} \\
\emph{actividad} & \emph{-dad} $\to$ \textbf{-ty} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\emph{The literary community has an extraordinary tradition. Its structure is voluntary, evidently, but the activity is enormous.}

\textbf{Nine words. Eight fell to rules you hold}, and the ninth is below.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what actually changed}]
The endings were never the point. This is:

\textbf{A paragraph of unfamiliar Spanish is no longer a wall.} Most of it is words you already know, wearing clothes you have learned to recognise. That change of expectation is worth more than any single word, because it is what lets you read above your level and get most of it — which is how the rest of the language arrives.

\emph{Enorme} is the ninth, and no ending gives it to you. You guessed it anyway, from \textbf{enormous}, and the guess was right. That is what the rules are really for: they do not decode every word, they make the guessing \textbf{safe}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the paragraph, out loud, all of it
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many of those words appear anywhere else in this book? (\textbf{None.}) How many did you read? (\textbf{All of them.}) And what is the real change? (An unfamiliar paragraph is \textbf{no longer a wall}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
